study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized cortical thickness asymmetry in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Schizophrenia

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) as described by Fraza et al. (2021) was used to establish normative ranges, accounting for both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Subsequently, we used Bayesian Linear Regression (Fraza et al., 2021).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Whole brain and regional (160 parcels) cortical thickness asymmetry index (AI), calculated as (LH - RH) / ((LH + RH) / 2).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We then computed the whole brain hemispheric Asymmetry Index (AI) for cortical thickness ... We then computed the AI for cortical thickness for each hemispheric region (r)
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Echave2024.pdf.md: Methods / Cortical thickness hemispheric Asymmetry Index

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age, sex, Euler number (FreeSurfer surface quality proxy), and scanner were used as predictors in the normative model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: established a normative range for AI, considering an individual's age, sex, Euler number, and scanner.
